main_strengths: Tool honesty is fixed: no backdrop value before get_macro_data, no value of an unrequested indicator, and no episode id the tool did not return (0/18). Every real-rate subtraction and every quoted probability sum is correct.

Analogs are weighed, not just listed: each item says which returned episodes fit and where they differ, and uses misfits for a limited point (Terra had no reserve portfolio; the Credit Suisse AT1 write-off as partial loss allocation; the 2008 China package far larger than 150bn; the zero floor vs the 1998 cuts; EP-2023-07-01 as a warning against calling a fast collapse).

School fidelity is high and specific to each event: the add-or-remove-intervention test runs through every item, with one or two fitting mechanisms each: relative-price vs monetary inflation (lithium), Cantillon via the exchange rate (BoE, BoJ), moral hazard (bank merger), private money substitutes (stablecoin), price-system breakdown (hyperinflation).

Data can overturn the prior: in 5 items a positive real rate turns the boom reading into a correction or a contained shock. Gold is SHORT twice and NEUTRAL once with explicit arithmetic ('the school's usual preference for hard assets must yield to the arithmetic').

Good news is handled better: the productivity jump, dovish BoE, YCC and BoJ purchases get equities LONG; the GDP beat and the China stimulus get equities NEUTRAL. Signal reasons mostly weigh named scenario sums, and S1-only reasoning survives in one item (syn-a0010).

The v2 prompt echoes are gone ('the event gives no bp', 'newest information', 'a single backdrop' in 0/18), and the weakest-link lines name a real missing input (foreign data, the policy reaction function, the reserve portfolio).
main_problems: Gold LONG 15/18 and credit SHORT 15/18 (v2 had gold LONG in 15/19). Conviction is lower (gold LONG 4 in 4 items vs 11 in v2), but the direction is unchanged. Gold is argued from the event and data in 3 items (dovish BoE, bank rescue, hyperinflation) and partly in 6 (a backdrop real rate or a minority debasement branch). It is a default in 6 (rents, lithium closure, productivity, Chinese default, 5% lithium tariff, BoJ purchases), and 4 of the LONGs come at clearly positive real rates (+0.9% to +4.9%). Credit SHORT is justified by the event in 5 items, partly in 5, and a default in 5 (GDP beat, productivity, lithium closure, 5% tariff, YCC). The template's 'Typical stance: favours hard assets and expects corrections after credit booms' outweighs 'No asset has a default direction, gold included'.

New failure mode: a signal takes the school's direction from a minority scenario and cuts conviction to 2-3 instead of going NEUTRAL. Examples: bonds or credit from S3 at 0.25 (syn-a0004, syn-a0014); gold from S2 at 0.30-0.37 against 0.63-0.70 (syn-a0009, syn-a0013); credit SHORT against 0.55 of compression (syn-a0006).

Prompt echo: the instruction 'say so in one sentence and weigh the event more' produces an event-vs-data 'tension' resolved for the event in 18/18 items ('weigh the event' 16/18, 'the event dominates' 2/18). The tension is often manufactured (syn-a0004, syn-a0013) or contradicts the item's own sizing of a small event (syn-a0010, syn-a0019). 'This school' self-reference appears in 17/18.

Templated numbers: 0.45/0.30/0.25 appears in 4 items, and 10/18 items share an exact probability tuple with another item. S1 is 0.45 in 7/18 and between 0.40 and 0.50 in 15/18. 'Confidence: moderate' appears in 18/18. 0.55/0.25/0.20 is gone, but the v1 tuple 0.45/0.30/0.15/0.10 returns once.

One-formula diagnosis: policy rate minus CPI is the deciding test in 18/18 ('artificially cheap' in 17/18), and the natural rate appears once. A past cheap-credit boom is asserted where the data show none (lithium closure, interbank stress, EM peg), and a +0.2% real rate is called 'effectively free'.

US backdrop misapplied to foreign events: the US real rate is used to judge the BoE and the RBA, US zero-bound QE is assumed as the answer to a Chinese default, and the pre-existing US backdrop is read as the new BoJ peg's effect. EP-2016-09 is taken as 'the event itself' although a 2023 episode came back in the same result.

Economic slips: a weaker yen said to raise US import prices (sign error); front end up and long end down called steepening; time preference direction reversed; 'forced saving' in a tightening; the real rate misread with negative core PCE; M2 at 6.5% with 0.4% CPI called 'not expansionary'.

Grounding slips: an invented rate cut; episode details merged (SVB vs Continental Illinois); a fiscal mini-budget used as the analog for monetary loosening; EP-2020-07 as a misfit analog; claims beyond the tools (2006 rents, late-1990s 'same configuration'). Some items signal assets they never fetched: oil SHORT with an unseen $112 WTI, equities and credit LONG with unseen -3.5% GDP and VIX 35, 'growth up' with unseen -6.0% GDP. The Proof has 8 lines in 3/18, omits the modal scenario once and gives no support for a top-conviction gold call once.
suggested_prompt_or_template_changes: Austrian 'Typical stance': drop 'favours hard assets and expects corrections after credit booms'. Replace it with a conditional: 'hard assets gain when real rates are negative and money is being created, and lose when real rates are positive and the event is deflationary; a correction needs a credit boom that the data show'.
Replace 'say so in one sentence and weigh the event more' with 'if the data really contradict the event, say which you trust and why; do not invent a tension'. Warn when a batch repeats the phrase.

Signal rule: sign each signal by its probability-weighted direction. When the scenarios for and against are within about 0.2 of each other, use NEUTRAL, and do not let a reason rest only on scenarios totalling under 0.4. Batch check: warn when one direction exceeds 60% for any asset within a school (gold, credit).

Probabilities and confidence: reject an exact probability tuple used more than twice per batch, and warn when S1 is between 0.40 and 0.50 in over half the items. Define the confidence levels (high: event, analog and data agree; low: the deciding datum is missing or the analogs misfit) and warn when one level exceeds 70%.
Austrian diagnosis: add 'compare the real rate with trend growth and productivity (the natural rate), not only with zero' and 'do not assume a past credit boom unless the data or the event show one'.

Foreign events: add 'the backdrop is US; do not use the US policy rate to judge a foreign central bank; name the foreign variable you lack'. In the episode DB, drop or label episodes that duplicate the event (BoJ YCC -> EP-2016-09), and state that the event comes after every returned episode.
Define asset referents and scale: equities = broad US index; credit = US high yield (or add an EM credit line). A sector-level shock needs a stated macro channel before any non-NEUTRAL broad call.

Data and Proof checks: require get_macro_data to include the indicator behind any signal of conviction 3 or more (WTI for oil, GDP for growth labels), or simply return the full backdrop. Enforce 4-7 Proof lines, an L5 line for the modal scenario, and a Proof line for every signal of conviction 3 or more.
Rephrase 'as this school reads it' in the prompt so the student does not learn to write 'in this school's terms' (17/18).
